Internships

Quantitative Researcher Intern, Shengshi Investment, Beijing, China (Mar. to July 2024)
  • Developed over 50 factors using 1-minute and tick level historical market data, yielding daily returns over 0.1%
  • Used jump-diffusion process to identify jumps in stock prices and developed market factors accordingly
  • Constructed portfolios based on market values and stock styles, then conducted multi-factor investing on them using multivariable linear regression and MLP neural networks; improved overall factor performance by 20%
Quantitative Researcher Intern, Luxtech Capital Group Ltd., Shenzhen, China (June to Sept. 2023)
  • Analyzed technical analysis indicators such as KDJ and RSI to design investment signals and factors
  • Applied the ARMA model to analyze trends in prices and developed high-frequency factors, then smoothed factor values using the exponentially weighted moving average model, yielding ICs from 0.05 to 0.1
  • Improved efficiency of algorithms, shortening their running time and reducing their working memory
Quantitative Researcher Intern, Commando Capital, Beijing, China (Jan. to May 2023)
  • Leveraged Python’s Numpy, Pandas, and Scipy to calculate and filter annual stock profit, and normalized it on a cross-sectional scale for use as a momentum factor
  • Designed trading signals that recognized the trends of stock prices and designed signals that bought or sold stocks accordingly, earning annual excessive returns ranging from 8% to 17%
  • Identified a pattern for potentially profitable stocks using normalized historical annual profit, maximum drawdown, and market capital, using it to select stocks that yielded significant returns

Academic Projects

Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence Project, Peking U., Beijing, China (Jan. to May 2022)
  • Participated in a team effort and used features such as location, size, amenities, and historical pricing data to identify key factors influencing housing prices and developed a predictive model
  • Plotted a heatmap of said features’ correlation matrix, discerning potential multicollinearity within the data
  • Fitted above features on housing prices using Linear, Ridge, Lasso, Polynomial, and XGBoost regression models, earning maximum scores of 0.94 on the training set and 0.85 on the test set
Financial Modeling and Quantitative Methods Project, Peking U., Beijing, China (Sept. to Dec. 2021)
  • Analyzed and recreated the three soldiers and crows candlestick patterns in classic quantitative trading strategies, earning a 15% annual average rate of return
  • Designed new parameters that can identify the patterns more flexibly and adjust the frequency of the investments

item.title: About Me
item.description:
My name is Shunran (Rebecca) He, and I am currently a Master of Financial Engineering student at Cornell University’s School of Operations Research and Information Engineering. I obtained my undergraduate degree from Peking University’s School of Economics, majoring in finance.

Professional Interests

I am interested in pursuing a career in quantitative finance, leveraging my strong foundation in advanced coursework and hands-on internship experience. My academic training not only includes mathematical and programming courses such as Stochastic Analysis, Monte Carlo Simulation, Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence, and Data Structure and Algorithm, but also financial application courses such as Fixed Income Securities, Financial Derivatives, Financial Modeling and Quantitative Methods, Financial Risk Management. During internships at Shengshi Investment, Luxtech Capital, and Commando Capital, I developed high-frequency trading signals, optimized multi-factor portfolios using ML techniques, and designed strategies yielding annual excess returns of up to 17%. These experiences have equipped me with the technical skills (Python, C++, MATLAB) and quantitative intuition to thrive in roles like quant research or algorithmic trading.
